skill.name: gh-axi
skill.description: Operate GitHub through gh-axi for issues, pull requests, CI, workflows, releases, repositories, Projects, gists, secrets, variables, search, and API access.
skill.summary: Use the gh-axi CLI to manage common and advanced GitHub workflows.
skill.author: Kun Chen (kunchenguid)

security_audit.summary: Two Markdown references are false positives because backticks only format CLI names. Three examples invoke an unpinned npm package through npx -y, creating remote code execution and supply-chain exposure.

remediation.issue: The examples execute an unpinned npm package with npx -y.
remediation.suggestion: Pin gh-axi to a reviewed version and require user confirmation before downloading or executing it.

content.value_statement: GitHub work often requires many commands across issues, pull requests, CI, releases, and projects. This skill directs agents to gh-axi for current commands and task execution.
actual_capabilities: Directs agents to the gh-axi dashboard and built-in help for current guidance.
Supports issue, pull request, review, merge, and stacked branch workflows.
Covers CI runs, workflow triggers, releases, repositories, and labels.
Supports gists, GitHub Projects, Actions secrets, and Actions variables.
Includes GitHub search and raw API access within its stated scope.
limitations: The skill file does not document individual command flags or complete workflows.
Operation requires the external gh-axi npm package and suitable GitHub authentication.
Available actions remain limited by the authenticated account and repository permissions.
The provided npx examples do not pin a reviewed package version.

use_cases.title: Review Repository Activity
use_cases.description: Summarize open pull requests, failing checks, and active issues before a planning session.

use_cases.title: Manage Stacked Changes
use_cases.description: Create and maintain related branches and pull requests for a multi-stage implementation.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Releases
use_cases.description: Inspect workflow runs, trigger approved automation, and prepare a GitHub release.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Repository Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-axi to inspect the current repository. Summarize open pull requests, failing checks, and urgent issues. Do not modify anything.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-axi to draft an issue for [problem]. Include expected behavior, observed behavior, and acceptance criteria. Show the draft before creating it.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-axi to inspect pull request [number]. Summarize changes, review status, CI results, and merge blockers. Do not merge without confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Stacked Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-axi to assess branches [branches], their pull requests, CI runs, project items, and release readiness. Propose an ordered action plan before changes.

output_examples.input: Summarize the current repository without making changes.
output_examples.output: Repository status: two open pull requests, one failing CI check, and three active issues. Pull request 42 is blocked by tests.

output_examples.input: Review pull request 42 and identify merge blockers.
output: Review status: one approval and one requested change.
Checks: unit tests failed; lint and build passed.
Merge blocker: resolve the requested change and rerun unit tests.

output_examples.output: Release readiness: the target milestone is complete, but one workflow remains unsuccessful. No release action was taken.

best_practices: Start with read-only inspection and summarize findings before applying changes.
Confirm destructive, publishing, merging, secret, and workflow-triggering actions with the user.
Use current CLI help and pin the reviewed gh-axi package version.
anti_patterns: Do not merge pull requests or publish releases without explicit confirmation.
Do not expose secrets, tokens, or sensitive variable values in responses.
Do not assume command flags from stale skill text when current CLI help is available.

faq.question: What GitHub work does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers issues, pull requests, CI, workflows, releases, repositories, labels, gists, Projects, secrets, variables, search, and API access.

faq.question: Does the skill include complete command documentation?
faq.answer: No. It directs the agent to the installed CLI dashboard and help output for current guidance.

faq.question: Does gh-axi require GitHub authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. GitHub operations require valid authentication and permissions appropriate for each requested action.

faq.question: Can it manage stacked pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. Stacked branches and pull requests are included in the skill's stated scope.

faq.question: Can it change Actions secrets and variables?
faq.answer: Yes, when the authenticated account has permission. Sensitive values should never appear in summaries or logs.

faq.question: Why should the npm package version be pinned?
faq.answer: Pinning limits unexpected changes and reduces exposure to compromised or incompatible future package releases.
